messages:
Anna (Support): FYI we just got an escalation from AcmeCorp. Their summarize_long_reports route has been producing "more generic" single-paragraph outputs since last night. They included before/after examples. They say it used to produce multi-bullet summaries with citations and now it's terse.

Anna (Support): Customer paste: "Before (last week):
- Key finding A: ...
- Recommendation: ...
After (this morning):
The report shows that A happened and recommends follow-up."

Anna (Support): Repro steps they sent (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-rlhf-v1","input":"<long report>","route":"summarize_long_reports"}'
```
They didn't set temperature/top_p explicitly.

Liam (Eng): Thanks Anna. Can you paste the exact customer request/route + the model name (they included model). I'll check recent rollouts. Which org id?

Anna (Support): Org: acmecorp-prod. Model: redwood-rlhf-v1. Route: summarize_long_reports. They started seeing the change ~2026-03-12 02:30 UTC (matches our nightly canary window).

DeployBot: Deploy event: rollout_id=rb-2026-03-12-02:12, services: hosted-runtime, affected_routes: summarize_long_reports (canary->global), diff: sampling.defaults.temperature: 0.9 -> 0.0, sampling.defaults.top_p: 0.95 -> 0.0.

Liam (Eng): Wait what. Who approved that change? That looks like someone forced greedy sampling defaults (temp=0, top_p=0) in the rollout config. I'll pull config history.

Javier (Research): Greedy defaults would definitely collapse variety and make responses shorter/less creative. Could explain the loss of bullet lists and citations. If the customer request didn't set sampling params, they'd inherit defaults.

Sarah (CSM): AcmeCorp is pretty sensitive to summary quality. They're on a paid plan and flagged this as "severity: high". They want fast remediation + root cause.

Liam (Eng): I found the change. In rollout rb-2026-03-12-02:12 the file sampling_migration.json was applied. Diff excerpt: 
```
- "sampling": {"temperature": 0.9, "top_p": 0.95}
+ "sampling": {"temperature": 0.0, "top_p": 0.0}
```
It looks like an unintended default for safety mode was flipped on and propagated to hosted defaults for that model route. The PR was authored by infra/safety-migration@ci-bot (auto-merge).

OpsOncall: We should rollback the default change for hosted runtime ASAP for that route. Can we do a targeted rollback to restore sampling defaults to 0.9/0.95 for summarize_long_reports without affecting other routes?

Liam (Eng): Yes -- we have config scoping by route. I'll create a hotfix rollout to restore previous sampling.defaults for redwood-rlhf-v1:summarize_long_reports. DeployBot, can you queue a rollback patch rb-hotfix-176912 for hosted-runtime?

DeployBot: Queued hotfix: rb-hotfix-176912. Target: hosted-runtime. Patch: sampling.defaults.temperature: 0.9; sampling.defaults.top_p: 0.95. Canary starting now.

Anna (Support): I notified AcmeCorp that we're investigating and will update in 30m. They've provided a new sample request for verification.

DeployBot: Canary passed (canary nodes: 2/2). Global roll started. Rollout complete at 1769123650.

Liam (Eng): Confirmed config now shows sampling.defaults.temperature=0.9/top_p=0.95 on hosted runtime for that route. Logging shows requests from acmecorp-prod now getting the old defaults.

Sarah (CSM): I asked AcmeCorp to re-run their tests. They replied within 12m: "Looks back to normal, bullets restored, thanks." :tada:

Anna (Support): Customer is satisfied for now but asked for RCA and to avoid silent defaults changes. They want notification for any future sampling-related rollouts that touch their routes.

Javier (Research): Root cause summary: an automated migration intended to apply a safety mode profile to a subset of routes accidentally matched and mutated the global defaults for hosted runtime for the redwood-rlhf-v1 summarize_long_reports route. The migration had a scoping bug in the selector logic (regex matched too broadly).

Liam (Eng): Action items (assigned):
- Liam: postmortem + fix selector logic in migration (patched, tests added).
- Javier: add unit/regression test that ensures default sampling values don't flip unexpectedly for routes that don't opt in.
- OpsOncall: add alert when sampling default changes are deployed for any customer-facing route.
- Support+CS: Sarah/Anna to inform customers affected and offer credits if needed.

DeployBot: New alert created: sampling-default-change (severity=warning). Hooked to #eng-oncall and #support.

Liam (Eng): PR merged for migration fix. CI shows added tests that simulate route selectors and fail on broad matches. Will schedule one more small canary in staging before making the migration pipeline stricter.

Anna (Support): AcmeCorp asked for the timestamp of the fix for their audit — gave them rollback completion ts 1769123650 and the upcoming PR link. They're happy with the communication.

Sarah (CSM): Posting a short summary to customers list and adding a blurb to release notes about not changing sampling defaults unless explicitly intended.

Liam (Eng): Closing thread once postmortem is posted. Thanks everyone.

Anna (Support): Closing: confirmed fix, customer validated. Postmortem link: https://redwood.internal/pm/rb-176912-postmortem (pending).
